definitions.explanation: A long, snake-like freshwater fish prized in Japanese cuisine, especially when grilled with a sweet soy-based sauce (kabayaki).

examples.japanese: {夏|なつ}バテ{防止|ぼうし}に{鰻|うなぎ}を{食|た}べる。
examples.english: I eat eel to prevent summer fatigue.

examples.japanese: {鰻|うなぎ}の{蒲焼|かばや}きは{日本|にほん}の{伝統料理|でんとうりょうり}だ。
examples.english: Grilled eel (kabayaki) is a traditional Japanese dish.

examples.japanese: {土用|どよう}の{丑|うし}の{日|ひ}に{鰻|うなぎ}を{食|た}べる{習慣|しゅうかん}がある。
examples.english: There's a custom of eating eel on the Day of the Ox during doyo.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
Eating {鰻|うなぎ} is especially associated with {土用|どよう}の{丑|うし}の{日|ひ} (Day of the Ox during the hottest period of summer), believed to provide stamina and prevent heat exhaustion.

COMMON DISHES:
・{鰻|うなぎ}の{蒲焼|かばや}き (grilled eel with sweet sauce)
・うな{重|じゅう} (eel over rice in a lacquer box)
・うな{丼|どん} (eel rice bowl)
・{白焼|しらや}き (plain grilled eel without sauce)
・ひつまぶし (Nagoya-style eel rice)

NOTE ON SUSTAINABILITY:
Japanese eel ({日本|にほん}ウナギ) is classified as endangered. Conservation efforts are ongoing.
